another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I have one child - my son Alex, he's 8 years old and lives with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask a few more questions.

Do you currently live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK at the moment. I'm living abroad right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since you're living abroad, your eligibility may depend on which country you're in and your circumstances.

Which country are you currently living in?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Since you're living in Spain, there are specific circumstances under which you might still be able to claim UK Child Benefit while abroad.

Could you tell me:
1. Are you a Crown servant (such as a diplomat or member of HM Forces posted abroad)?
2. Or are you an EU/EEA national or do you have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not a Crown servant - I'm not working for the government or in the forces or anything like that. And no, I don't have any of that EU settlement status stuff either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that information.

Just to confirm - are you a British citizen who has moved to Spain, or do you have a different nationality?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen, yes. I just moved to Spain.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming. I have one more important question:

Are you or your partner working in the UK and paying UK National Insurance contributions, or do you have any other ongoing connection to the UK such as being temporarily posted abroad by a UK employer?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, neither of us are working in the UK or paying National Insurance there. We've just moved here to Spain - no UK employment connection at all.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm sorry to inform you that you are **not eligible** for UK Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why: While you would normally qualify for Child Benefit since Alex is your 8-year-old son who lives with you, the issue is that you're currently living in Spain. 

According to UK Child Benefit rules, you can only claim Child Benefit while living abroad in specific circumstances, such as:
- Being a Crown servant (diplomat or HM Forces member posted abroad)
- Having certain EU Settlement Scheme statuses with qualifying conditions
- Having ongoing UK employment and National Insurance connections

Since you've moved to Spain without any of these qualifying connections to the UK, you don't meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit while living abroad.

If your circumstances change in the future - for example, if you move back to the UK - you would then be able to claim Child Benefit for Alex.
